title: Music & Recording
tagline: How recorded sound went from wax to streaming.
source: Curated; audio engineering history and Wikipedia.

events.title: The phonograph is conceived
events.text: Thomas Edison invents the phonograph, the first device able to both record and replay sound.

events.title: The long-playing record
events.text: Columbia introduces the 33⅓ rpm LP, doubling album durations and transforming the music business.

references.label: Columbia Records introduces LP on June 18, 1948

events.title: The compact cassette
events.text: Philips launches the cassette tape, portable recorded music for the masses.

events.title: The CD: digital sound arrives
events.text: Sony and Philips release the compact disc, bringing digital audio to consumers and triggering CD’s dominance.

events.title: Napster: the internet disrupts music
events.text: Napster’s peer-to-peer file sharing makes sharing music effortless, forcing a reinvention of the industry.

events.title: The iPod and iTunes
events.text: Apple launches the iPod and iTunes, legitimising legal digital downloads and coining the phrase “put a thousand songs in your pocket”.

events.title: Streaming becomes king
events.text: Streaming platforms overtake digital downloads and physical formats to become the dominant way music is consumed worldwide.
